changes.before: Former Residence of Xiao Jun (蜗蜗居)

changes.zh: 蒋介石北平行辕旧址即后圆恩寺胡同7号宅院，官方旧文称其原为清宗室载旉宅第，建筑坐北朝南并具有中西合璧特点。抗战胜利后，资料记载该宅院自1945年12月至1949年1月成为蒋介石在北平的行辕；期间他曾来平慰问北方同胞，并于1948年9月在此应付辽沈战役。另一篇官方旧文称，1948年后该院迎来新主人“中共中央华北局办公处”。上述均为历史使用信息，不等同于当前开放状态。
changes.before: The former site of Chiang Kai-shek’s Beiping headquarters is the residence at No. 7 Houyuan’en Temple Hutong. An official historical text states that it was originally the residence of the Qing imperial clansman Zai Fu, with the building oriented north–south and featuring a combination of Chinese and Western characteristics. After the victory of the War of Resistance, the materials record that the residence served as Chiang Kai-shek’s headquarters in Beiping from December 1945 to January 1949. During this period he visited Beiping to express concern for compatriots in the north, and in September 1948 dealt with the Liaoshen Campaign there. Another official historical text states that after 1948 the compound received a new occupant, the “Office of the Central Committee’s North China Bureau.” These are historical uses and do not indicate its current access status.
changes.after: The former site of Chiang Kai-shek’s Beiping headquarters is the residence at No. 7 Houyuan’en Temple Hutong. An official historical text states that it was originally the residence of the Qing imperial clansman Zai Fu, with the building facing south and featuring a combination of Chinese and Western characteristics. Another official historical text states that after 1948 the compound received a new occupant, the “Office of the Central Committee’s North China Bureau.” These are historical uses and do not indicate its current access status.

changes.zh: 黑芝麻胡同13号据文旅旧文曾为清朝刑部尚书奎俊的宅邸。现有来源没有进一步说明宅院的建造年代、格局、保存状态或现今使用方式，因此本条仅作历史宅主归属的资料整理。
changes.before: According to a historical cultural-tourism text, No. 13 Heizhima Hutong was once the residence of Kui Jun, a Minister of the Board of Punishments in the Qing dynasty. Existing sources provide no further information on the residence’s construction date, layout, state of preservation, or present use. This entry therefore only整理ates the source’s record of its historical owner.

changes.zh: 广化寺位于鸦儿胡同31号，始建于元代，明成化、万历及清代道光、咸丰、光绪年间多次重修。寺院坐北朝南，主要建筑沿中轴线分布，包括影壁、山门殿、天王殿、大雄宝殿和藏经阁；西侧有观音阁、地藏阁、方丈室、法堂、祖堂等院落，东路尚存两层殿，其余部分已有拆改。藏经阁所载资料包括明版《大藏经》、清乾隆版《频伽藏》和东瀛版《续藏》。寺院还曾用于京师图书馆、佛学院和小学等事项，1982年北京市佛教协会设于此。
changes.before: Guanghua Temple is located at No. 31 Yao’er Hutong. It was first built during the Yuan dynasty and repeatedly rebuilt during the Chenghua and Wanli periods of the Ming dynasty and the Daoguang, Xianfeng, and Guangxu periods of the Qing dynasty. The temple faces south, with its principal buildings arranged along the central axis, including a spirit wall, mountain-gate hall, Hall of the Heavenly Kings, Mahavira Hall, and Sutra Repository. On the west are courtyards containing the Guanyin Pavilion, Kṣitigarbha Pavilion, abbot’s quarters, Dharma hall, and ancestral hall; two two-story halls remain on the eastern route, while the rest has been demolished or altered. Materials recorded in the Sutra Repository include the Ming edition of the Tripitaka, the Qianlong edition of the Pinqie Canon, and the Japanese edition of the Supplementary Canon. The temple also served at various times as the Jingshi Library, a Buddhist academy, and a primary school. In 1982, the Beijing Buddhist Association was established there.
changes.after: Guanghua Temple is located at No. 31 Ya’er Hutong. It was first built during the Yuan dynasty and repeatedly rebuilt during the Chenghua and Wanli periods of the Ming dynasty and the Daoguang, Xianfeng, and Guangxu periods of the Qing dynasty. The temple faces south, with its principal buildings arranged along the central axis, including a spirit wall, mountain-gate hall, Hall of the Heavenly Kings, Mahavira Hall, and Sutra Repository. On the west are courtyards containing the Guanyin Pavilion, Kṣitigarbha Pavilion, abbot’s quarters, Dharma hall, and ancestral hall; a two-storey hall remains on the eastern route, while the rest has been demolished or altered. Materials recorded in the Sutra Repository include the Ming edition of the Tripitaka, the Qianlong edition of the Pinqie Canon, and the Japanese edition of the Supplementary Canon. The temple also served at various times as the Jingshi Library, a Buddhist academy, and a primary school. In 1982, the Beijing Buddhist Association was established there.

changes.zh: 醇亲王府（北府）位于后海北沿44号，原为明珠府，乾隆年间改为成亲王府，1888年迁为醇亲王府，因区别于鲍家街的旧府而称“北府”。清宣统帝溥仪出生于此，其父载沣被称为摄政王。府邸坐北朝南，东部为府邸，西部为花园；资料列举府邸中的银安殿、宝翰堂、九思堂、思谦堂等建筑。西花园后来改作宋庆龄故居。
changes.before: Prince Chun’s Residence (Northern Residence) is located at No. 44 along the northern shore of Houhai. It was originally the residence of Mingzhu, became Prince Cheng’s Residence during the Qianlong period, and was transferred to Prince Chun’s Residence in 1888. It was called the “Northern Residence” to distinguish it from the former residence on Baoji Street. The Xuantong Emperor Puyi of the Qing dynasty was born here, and his father Zai Feng was known as the regent. The residence faces south, with the residence compound in the east and a garden in the west. Sources list buildings including Yinan Hall, Baohan Hall, Jiusi Hall, and Siqian Hall. The Western Garden was later converted into the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence.
changes.after: Prince Chun’s Residence (Northern Residence) is located at No. 44 along the northern shore of Houhai. It was originally the residence of Mingzhu, became Prince Cheng’s Residence during the Qianlong period, and was transferred to Prince Chun’s Residence in 1888. It was called the “Northern Residence” to distinguish it from the former residence on Baojia Street. The Xuantong Emperor Puyi of the Qing dynasty was born here, and his father Zai Feng was known as the regent. The residence faces south, with the residence compound in the east and a garden in the west. Sources list buildings including Yin’an Hall, Baohan Hall, Jiusi Hall, and Siqian Hall. The Western Garden was later converted into the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence.

changes.zh: 涛贝勒府位于柳荫街27号，涛贝勒载涛为醇贤亲王奕譞第七子、摄政王载沣之弟。府址原为康熙帝十五子允禑的愉王府，清末改为载涛府邸。府坐北朝南，北部为府邸、南部为花园，府邸分中东​​西三路，花园设长廊、亭、花厅、假山和马厩。1925年租给罗马教廷作为辅仁大学校址，府邸部分后作辅仁男中；1952年相关院落拆平建设教学楼和操场，现中路、东路部分院落仍存王府风貌。
changes.before: Prince Tao’s Residence is located at No. 27 Liuyin Street. Prince Tao Zai Tao was the seventh son of Prince Chun Xian Yixuan and the younger brother of the regent Zai Feng. The site was originally the residence of Yinyu, the fifteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor, and was converted into Zai Tao’s residence in the late Qing period. The residence faces south, with the residential compound in the north and a garden in the south. The compound was divided into central, eastern, and western routes; the garden had a covered corridor, pavilions, a flower hall, rockeries, and stables. In 1925 it was rented to the Holy See as the site of Fu Jen University, and part of the residence later became Fu Jen Boys’ Middle School. In 1952, related courtyards were leveled to build teaching buildings and sports grounds; some courtyards on the central and eastern routes still retain the character of a princely residence.
changes.after: Beile Zaitao’s Residence is located at No. 27 Liuyin Street. Beile Zaitao was the seventh son of Prince Chun Xian Yixuan and the younger brother of the regent Zai Feng. The site was originally the residence of Yinyu, the fifteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor, and was converted into Zai Tao’s residence in the late Qing period. The residence faces south, with the residential compound in the north and a garden in the south. The compound was divided into central, eastern, and western routes; the garden had a covered corridor, pavilions, a flower hall, rockeries, and stables. In 1925 it was rented to the Holy See as the site of Fu Jen University, and part of the residence later became Fu Jen Boys’ Middle School. In 1952, related courtyards were leveled to build teaching buildings and sports grounds; some courtyards on the central and eastern routes still retain the character of a princely residence.

changes.zh: 辅仁大学旧址（定阜街主楼）位于定阜街1号，所在地原为涛贝勒府花园和马厩。1925年载涛将其租给罗马教廷，由美国天主教本笃会创办辅仁大学；1930年在空地和马厩处建成中西合璧的教学主楼。主楼曾设教室、实验室、图书馆、办公室及可容纳千人的礼堂。1952年辅仁大学与北京师范大学合并，主楼改作北师大化学系校舍。
changes.before: The Former Site of Fu Jen University (Main Building on Dingfu Street) is located at No. 1 Dingfu Street. The site originally comprised the garden and stables of Prince Tao’s Residence. In 1925, Zai Tao rented it to the Holy See, and Fu Jen University was founded by the American Catholic Benedictines. In 1930, a Chinese-Western-style main teaching building was completed on the vacant land and at the stables. The building once contained classrooms, laboratories, a library, offices, and an auditorium accommodating 1,000 people. In 1952, Fu Jen University merged with Beijing Normal University, and the main building became the premises of the chemistry department of Beijing Normal University.
changes.after: The Former Site of Fu Jen University (Main Building on Dingfu Street) is located at No. 1 Dingfu Street. The site originally comprised the garden and stables of Beile Zaitao’s Residence. In 1925, Zai Tao rented it to the Holy See, and Fu Jen University was founded by the American Catholic Benedictines. In 1930, a Chinese-Western-style main teaching building was completed on the vacant land and at the stables. The building once contained classrooms, laboratories, a library, offices, and an auditorium accommodating 1,000 people. In 1952, Fu Jen University merged with Beijing Normal University, and the main building became the premises of the chemistry department of Beijing Normal University.

changes.zh: 鸦儿胡同属西城区什刹海街道，东南起小石碑胡同并与烟袋斜街相连，西北至甘露胡同。其名称沿革见于元代“沿儿胡同”、明代“广化寺街”，清代因谐音形成“鸭儿胡同”“鸦儿胡同”等称呼。胡同全长820米，沿线分布广化寺、宋庆龄故居及萧军故居“蜗蜗居”等文物或名人旧居。资料还记述，后海商业开发后，部分房舍改作酒吧，街巷环境和功能发生变化。
changes.before: Yao’er Hutong belongs to Shichahai Subdistrict, Xicheng District. It begins in the southeast at Xiaoshibei Hutong, connects with Yandai Xiejie, and extends northwest to Ganlu Hutong. Its name history includes “Yan’er Hutong” in the Yuan dynasty and “Guanghua Temple Street” in the Ming dynasty; in the Qing dynasty, the names “Ya’er Hutong” and “Yā’er Hutong” developed through phonetic similarity. The hutong is 820 meters long, with Guanghua Temple, the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence, and Xiao Jun’s former residence “Wowo Residence” among the heritage sites and former residences of notable figures along it. Sources also record that after commercial development around Houhai, some houses were converted into bars and the environment and functions of the lanes changed.
changes.after: Ya’er Hutong belongs to Shichahai Subdistrict, Xicheng District. It begins in the southeast at Xiaoshibei Hutong, connects with Yandai Xiejie, and extends northwest to Ganlu Hutong. Its name history includes “Yan’er Hutong” in the Yuan dynasty and “Guanghua Temple Street” in the Ming dynasty; in the Qing dynasty, the names “Ya’er Hutong” and “Yā’er Hutong” developed through phonetic similarity. The hutong is 820 meters long, with Guanghua Temple, the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence, and Xiao Jun’s former residence “Wowo Residence” among the heritage sites and former residences of notable figures along it. Sources also record that after commercial development around Houhai, some houses were converted into bars and the environment and functions of the lanes changed.

changes.zh: 德胜门箭楼位于西城区德胜门立交桥北侧，是明清北京内城九座城门之一。来源记载其建成于1439年，后经历不同程度的修建。箭楼坐南朝北，平面呈倒“凸”字形，面阔七间、进深两间，采用前楼后厦布局，屋顶为重檐歇山式绿琉璃剪边顶。资料将其列为明清北京城防设施，并作为研究古代都城建设、建筑营造技术及北京城市发展史的实物资料。
changes.before: The Deshengmen Arrow Tower is located north of the Deshengmen overpass in Xicheng District and is one of the nine gates of the inner city of Beijing during the Ming and Qing periods. Sources record that it was completed in 1439 and subsequently underwent construction and repair to varying degrees. The arrow tower faces south, has an inverted “凸”-shaped plan, seven bays in width and two bays in depth, and uses a front-tower/rear-extension layout. Its roof is a green-glazed tile roof with double eaves and a hip-and-gable form, edged with glazed tiles. Materials list it as a Ming-Qing city-defense facility and as physical material for studying ancient capital construction, architectural building techniques, and the history of Beijing’s urban development.
changes.after: The Deshengmen Arrow Tower is located north of the Deshengmen overpass in Xicheng District and is one of the nine gates of the inner city of Beijing during the Ming and Qing periods. Sources record that it was completed in 1439 and subsequently underwent construction and repair to varying degrees. The arrow tower faces north, has an inverted stepped and projecting plan, seven bays in width and two bays in depth, and uses a front-tower/rear-extension layout. It has a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof with green-glazed tile edging. Materials list it as a Ming-Qing city-defense facility and as physical material for studying ancient capital construction, architectural building techniques, and the history of Beijing’s urban development.

changes.zh: 萧军故居“蜗蜗居”位于鸦儿胡同6号院内，是一座木构西式二层小楼。官方资料称，萧军自1951年起在此居住，直至去世，期间创作了《五月的矿山》《吴越春秋史话》《第三代》等作品及多部书信集，也曾遭受文革时期的冲击。该处被列为北京市文物保护单位；官方旧文还记载，截至2005年初小楼已搬空。
changes.before: Xiao Jun’s Former Residence “Wowo Residence” is located within the compound at No. 6 Yao’er Hutong and is a small two-story Western-style timber building. Official materials state that Xiao Jun lived there from 1951 until his death. During this period he wrote works including The Mine in May, Historical Stories of the Spring and Autumn Periods of Wu and Yue, and The Third Generation, as well as several collections of letters; he also suffered persecution during the Cultural Revolution. The site is listed as a Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Site. An older official text also records that the building had been emptied by early 2005.
changes.after: Xiao Jun’s Former Residence “Wowo Residence” is located within the compound at No. 6 Ya’er Hutong and is a small two-story Western-style timber building. Official materials state that Xiao Jun lived there from 1951 until his death. During this period he wrote works including The Mine in May, Historical Stories of the Spring and Autumn Periods of Wu and Yue, and The Third Generation, as well as several collections of letters; he also suffered persecution during the Cultural Revolution. The site is listed as a Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Site. An older official text also records that the building had been emptied by early 2005.

changes.zh: 福字碑位于恭王府花园滴翠岩下的秘云洞内。官方资料称，碑身长129厘米、宽54厘米，碑面中央刻有字径59厘米×33厘米的“福”字，上方钤刻“康熙御笔之宝”。资料将其字形解释为兼含“子、才、寿、田”等意象，寓意多子、多才、多田、多寿及多福。
changes.before: The Stele of the “Fu” Character is located inside Miyun Cave beneath Dicu Rock in the garden of Prince Gong’s Residence. Official materials state that the stele is 129 centimeters long and 54 centimeters wide. At the center of its face is the character “Fu,” with character dimensions of 59 by 33 centimeters; above it is the seal inscription “Treasure of the Kangxi Emperor’s Imperial Brush.” Sources interpret the character’s form as incorporating the images of “子,” “才,” “寿,” and “田,” symbolizing many children, talents, fields, longevity, and blessings.
changes.after: The Stele of the “Fu” Character is located inside Miyun Cave beneath Dicui Rock in the garden of Prince Gong’s Residence. Official materials state that the stele is 129 centimeters long and 54 centimeters wide. At the center of its face is the character “Fu,” with character dimensions of 59 by 33 centimeters; above it is the seal inscription “Treasure of the Kangxi Emperor’s Imperial Brush.” Sources interpret the character’s form as incorporating the images of “zi (children),” “cai (talent),” “shou (longevity),” and “tian (fields),” symbolizing many children, talents, fields, longevity, and blessings.

changes.zh: 西洋门位于恭王府花园中路最南端，是花园正门。官方资料称，门体以汉白玉石雕砌，为西方洛可可式雕花石拱券门，融汇柱式、拱券、隆起顶部、贝壳和西洋花穗浮雕等装饰。门额外刻“静含太古”，内刻“秀挹恒春”，门两侧线法墙亦有精细浮雕，体现西式形式与本土文化装饰的结合。
changes.before: The Western Gate is located at the southernmost end of the central axis of the Garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion and is the main gate of the garden. Official sources state that the gate is built of carved white marble and is a Western Rococo-style carved stone arched gate, incorporating such decorative elements as classical orders, arches, a raised top, shells, and reliefs of Western floral sprays. The outer side of the gate lintel is carved with “静含太古,” and the inner side with “秀挹恒春.” The line-method walls on both sides of the gate also bear finely executed reliefs, demonstrating a combination of Western forms and local cultural decoration.
changes.after: The Western Gate is located at the southernmost end of the central axis of the Garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion and is the main gate of the garden. Official sources state that the gate is built of carved white marble and is a Western Rococo-style carved stone arched gate, incorporating such decorative elements as classical orders, arches, a raised top, shells, and reliefs of Western floral sprays. The outer side of the gate lintel is carved with “Jing han tai gu,” and the inner side with “Xiu yi heng chun.” The line-method walls on both sides of the gate also bear finely executed reliefs, demonstrating a combination of Western forms and local cultural decoration.

changes.zh: 多福轩位于恭王府府邸东路第三进院落，正殿五间，覆灰色筒瓦，东西各有耳房。殿内悬有慈禧太后为恭亲王奕䜣五十岁寿辰所赐的“同德延釐”匾额，四壁上方陈列“福”“寿”斗方，北墙设楠木大书架。顶棚彩绘以玉兰、海棠为题材，官网称屋梁还残留乾隆时期凤和玺彩画局部。门前庭院有一架百年以上藤萝，因此该院落又被称作“藤萝院”。
changes.before: Duofu Studio is located in the third courtyard of the eastern section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. The main hall is five bays wide and covered with gray tubular tiles, with side rooms to the east and west. Inside the hall hangs a plaque reading “同德延釐,” bestowed by Empress Dowager Cixi for Prince Gong Yixin’s fiftieth birthday. Square calligraphic panels bearing the characters “福” and “寿” are displayed above the four walls, and a large nanmu bookcase is set against the north wall. The painted ceiling features magnolias and crabapple blossoms. The official website states that remnants of Qianlong-period phoenix-and-seal polychrome painting remain on the beams. A wisteria over one hundred years old stands in the courtyard in front of the hall, and the courtyard is therefore also called the “Wisteria Courtyard.”
changes.after: Duofu Studio is located in the third courtyard of the eastern section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. The main hall is five bays wide and covered with gray tubular tiles, with side rooms to the east and west. Inside the hall hangs a plaque reading “Tong de yan xi,” bestowed by Empress Dowager Cixi for Prince Gong Yixin’s fiftieth birthday. Square calligraphic panels bearing the characters “fu (blessings)” and “shou (longevity)” are displayed above the four walls, and a large nanmu bookcase is set against the north wall. The painted ceiling features magnolias and crabapple blossoms. The official website states that remnants of Qianlong-period phoenix-and-seal polychrome painting remain on the beams. A wisteria over one hundred years old stands in the courtyard in front of the hall, and the courtyard is therefore also called the “Wisteria Courtyard.”

changes.zh: 独乐峰位于恭王府花园中路、西洋门北侧，是一块高约5米的北太湖石孤赏石。官网称其设置在花园入口附近，既用于点缀园林、遮挡视线，也兼具影壁和屏风作用。石体因多年风化形成自然纹理，原文将其形态比作软水漩涡或淡云舒卷。仰望时可见“乐峰”二字，而“独”字隐藏在石顶，构成其名称的视觉趣味。
changes.before: Dule Peak is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, north of the Western Gate. It is an approximately five-meter-high solitary ornamental rock of northern Taihu stone. The official website states that it was placed near the garden entrance both to embellish the landscape and block the view, while also serving as a screen wall and screen. Natural textures formed through years of weathering cover the stone; the original text compares its form to a whirlpool in soft water or thin clouds unfurling. When viewed from below, the two characters “乐峰” can be seen, while the character “独” is hidden at the top of the stone, creating a visual play on its name.
changes.after: Dule Peak is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, north of the Western Gate. It is an approximately five-meter-high solitary ornamental rock of northern Taihu stone. The official website states that it was placed near the garden entrance both to embellish the landscape and block the view, while also serving as a screen wall and screen. Natural textures formed through years of weathering cover the stone; the original text compares its form to a whirlpool in soft water or thin clouds unfurling. When viewed from below, the two characters “Le Feng” can be seen, while the character “Du” is hidden at the top of the stone, creating a visual play on its name.

changes.zh: 棣华轩位于恭王府花园中路蝠池东侧，因悬挂咸丰皇帝御书“棣华轩”匾额而得名。官网将其名称与奕詝、奕䜣幼年习练枪法和刀法的经历联系起来：道光皇帝曾赐枪法名“棣华协力”、刀法名“宝锷宣威”，并寄望兄弟协力。资料由此呈现了棣华轩名称所承载的宫廷家族寓意。
changes.before: Dihua Studio is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, east of the Bat Pond. It was named after the plaque inscribed by the Xianfeng Emperor in his own hand with “棣华轩.” The official website connects its name with the experiences of Yizhu and Yixin practicing spear and saber techniques in their youth: the Daoguang Emperor bestowed the name “Dihua United Effort” on the spear technique and “Treasure Edge Proclaiming Might” on the saber technique, expressing his hope that the brothers would work together. The sources thus present the courtly familial implications carried by the name Dihua Studio.
changes.after: Dihua Studio is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, east of the Bat Pond. It was named after the plaque inscribed by the Xianfeng Emperor in his own hand with “Dihua Xuan.” The official website connects its name with the experiences of Yizhu and Yixin practicing spear and saber techniques in their youth: the Daoguang Emperor bestowed the name “Dihua United Effort” on the spear technique and “Treasure Edge Proclaiming Might” on the saber technique, expressing his hope that the brothers would work together. The sources thus present the courtly familial implications carried by the name Dihua Studio.

changes.zh: 滴翠岩是一座以太湖石叠成的假山，位于恭王府花园中路安善堂北边；秘云洞藏在假山腹部，内有康熙御笔“福字碑”。滴翠岩顶部为园中制高处，设有“绿天小隐”和邀月台。名称据官网解释与山石间苔藓有关：过去蓄水后，夏秋间石壁生出翠绿苔藓，形成石黄苔绿、苍翠欲滴的景象。
changes.before: Dicu Rock is an artificial hill formed by stacking Taihu stones, located north of Anshan Hall in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion. Miyun Cave is concealed within the body of the artificial hill and contains a “福” character stele written by the Kangxi Emperor in his own hand. The top of Dicu Rock is the highest point in the garden, with the “Green Heaven Little Hermitage” and Moon-Inviting Terrace located there. According to the official website, the name is related to moss among the rocks: in the past, after water was stored, emerald-green moss grew on the rock walls in summer and autumn, forming a scene of yellow stone and green moss, lush and dripping with verdure.
changes.after: Dicui Rock is an artificial hill formed by stacking Taihu stones, located north of Anshan Hall in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion. Miyun Cave is concealed within the body of the artificial hill and contains a “fu (blessings)” character stele written by the Kangxi Emperor in his own hand. The top of Dicui Rock is the highest point in the garden, with the “Green Heaven Little Hermitage” and Moon-Inviting Terrace located there. According to the official website, the name is related to moss among the rocks: in the past, after water was stored, emerald-green moss grew on the rock walls in summer and autumn, forming a scene of yellow stone and green moss, lush and dripping with verdure.

本条依据滴翠岩页面中对秘云洞的直接记载，将秘云洞作为题名所含部分一并说明。原文未说明相关构筑物是原构、复建或陈列，也未说明当前可否进入。
changes.before:
The components of Prince Gong's Mansion listed on the official website are described individually according to the source text as original structures, reconstructions, or bases for display; no inference is made from the introduction pages about whether interiors can be entered or performances are held on the day in question.
This entry is based on the direct account of Miyun Cave on the page for Dicu Rock, and includes Miyun Cave as a component of the name. The original text does not state whether the related structures are original, reconstructed, or displayed, nor whether they can currently be entered.
